contextNote: A subagent with no memory of this session was briefed (read-only: tests, greps, read-only git, small node snippets) to falsify: the ledger's completeness across all four host-runner exit paths and its one-shot semantics; the reverse guard's false positives and false negatives; the picker against its own rule that Docker result order must never decide the target; the architecture review's ten contract invariants; and the test quality, including which acceptance criteria would stay green if the implementation were wrong.
executedBy: pi subagent — general-purpose agent, clean context, read-only

attempts.hypothesis: Every host attempt is counted and the first of a session is announced.
attempts.method: Traced all four exit paths in the host runner and inspected the ledger's lifetime.
attempts.evidence: The counting holds, but the notice fires on refused attempts and the ledger lives for the extension instance, so a reload resets it; the summary was ALSO never rendered by `/devcontainer status` because the optional parameter reached only one of its two call sites.

attempts.hypothesis: The reverse guard cannot wrongly refuse legitimate container work.
attempts.method: Constructed mirror mounts, container paths beneath the host path, prefix-sharing paths and flag values.
attempts.evidence: Two false refusals: a `mounts: source == target` mirror of the host path, and the container's own path whenever it sits beneath the host path (the guard refused the very path its remedy names).

attempts.hypothesis: A failure inside the new guard still lands on a channel someone reads.
attempts.method: Drove the real ExecutionService/TargetStore with a `mappingFor` that rejects.
attempts.evidence: `container-exec rejected: daemon-unavailable` with no audit write — the mapping read sat outside the audit boundary.

attempts.hypothesis: The picker preserves 'Docker order never decides'.
attempts.method: Read the ambiguous branch and checked the no-UI path, duplicate labels and empty candidate lists.
attempts.evidence: The rule holds; the missing `hasUI` guard (present on every other prompt in the file) and the id+state-only labels (the candidate type has no image) were the gaps.

attempts.hypothesis: The ledger cannot leak a credential.
attempts.method: Recorded `curl -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-live-…'` and read the summary.
attempts.evidence: The argv was stored verbatim and rendered to the operator, i.e. a plaintext copy of what the audit trail captures by fingerprint only.

attempts.hypothesis: The review's ten contract invariants did not move.
attempts.method: Compared the CLI argv, the gates, discovery timing, the audit shape and the setup path.
attempts.evidence: Host path to the CLI, argv shapes, `stop`/`remove` gates, withholding, setup, audit shape and 0600 all unchanged; discovery stayed lazy/read-only/bounded (only doubled on the guarded path).

findings.message: `/devcontainer status` did not receive the host-run summary (the optional parameter reached `/devcontainer list` only), so AC-1, the CHANGELOG, `docs/security.md` and a README row were false while the suite stayed green.

The reverse guard's mapping read (a registry read, hence `docker ps`) sat outside any audit boundary, so a Docker failure escaped with no record — breaking 'every failure path lands on a channel someone reads'.
A configuration that mirrors the host path into the container at its own path (`mounts: source == target`) was refused, and the container path was refused whenever it sat beneath the host path.
The container picker was the only prompt in its file without a `hasUI` guard, so a print/json run could have hung or thrown.
The ledger stored argv verbatim, so a credential would have been rendered in `/devcontainer status`.
The guard does not see routed-shell text, `~`-relative or symlinked spellings, or a host path belonging to another workspace — all false negatives (status quo).
The notice said 'first host command' for a command that may never have run; a refused attempt consumes the one-shot.
The new security section was inserted inside the gates table (orphaning rows), the English README listed `/devcontainer use` twice, and the Chinese README lacked the row.
